requirement: Fetch every distinct key once on a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor, collect results as futures complete, and record each failing key's exception as a type-and-message string without letting one failure abort the batch.
skeleton: Generic BatchReport dataclass with values and errors dicts built by default_factory, and fetch_all validating max_workers, submitting one future per distinct key, and draining as_completed into the report.
caption: Concurrent fan-out with the standard-library concurrent.futures module. BatchReport is a generic dataclass whose values dict maps a key to its result and whose errors dict maps a key to a formatted error, each created with field default_factory. fetch_all(keys, fetch, max_workers=4) raises ValueError saying max_workers must be at least 1 when the pool would be empty. Inside a ThreadPoolExecutor with that many workers it submits fetch once per distinct key, deduplicating with dict.fromkeys so the first-seen order is kept, and maps each Future back to its key. It iterates as_completed over the futures; for each one it stores future.result() under the key, or, when the call raised any Exception, stores the exception class name, a colon and the message under errors, so a KeyError for one key does not stop the rest. The executor context waits for all threads before the report is returned. The fixture asserts that a KeyError for b leaves A and C in values and records KeyError: 'b', that a repeated key is fetched only once, that at most two fetches overlap with two workers and four with the default, and that zero workers raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Look up many keys in parallel and see exactly which ones failed
constraints: The pool defaults to four workers
Each distinct key is fetched exactly once
A failing key is recorded as the exception name and message while other keys still succeed

rationale.teaches: ThreadPoolExecutor with a future-to-key map drained by as_completed, catching per-future exceptions into a keyed report.
rationale.why: Batch fetchers commonly let the first future.result() exception abort everything, repeat duplicate keys, or lose the exception type, and only a mixed batch with duplicates and a concurrency probe exposes all three.

ops.docstring: Fetch many keys on a thread pool and report each key's result or error.

ops.stmt: from concurrent.futures import Future, ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

candidates.why_wrong: Zero workers reach ThreadPoolExecutor, whose own ValueError does not say at least 1.
The default pool has one worker, so default batches run serially.
Duplicate keys are submitted again, so the same key is fetched twice.
Only str(exc) is stored, dropping the exception type from the error.
Only OSError is caught, so a KeyError from one key aborts the whole batch.
